name: North Carolina

jury_list.statute: N.C.G.S. 9-6.2(b): 'The list of persons requesting to be disqualified from jury duty due to lack of being a citizen of the United States shall be a public record, subject to G.S. 163-82.10(a1).' Also G.S. 163-82.14(c1)(3).
jury_list.holder: North Carolina State Board of Elections. The clerk of superior court's own records are NOT public records (G.S. 9-6.2(a)).
fields_withheld: full or partial Social Security number
jury_list.official_pipeline: G.S. 9-6.2(b): clerks send name, address, date of birth, reason and date of disqualification to the State Board. G.S. 163-82.14(c1): within 30 days the State Board reviews registration and citizenship status, drops anyone who became a citizen after the disqualification date, and sends county reports; counties give 30 days' notice before removal; an objection triggers a challenge under 163-85(c)(7).

sources.cite: N.C.G.S. 163-82.10(a1) (dates of birth and other PII confidential)

voter_file.who_may_get: Any person, from the county board of elections at cost (G.S. 163-82.10(c)). The State Board also publishes statewide voter registration files for download.
voter_file.permitted_uses: G.S. 163-82.10 states no purpose restriction for these lists. Lists may not contain date of birth (163-82.10(c)). Signatures may be viewed but not copied (163-82.10(a2)).

sources.cite: NCSBE - Voter Registration Data (statewide downloadable files)
NCSBE voter file layout (birth_year, age_at_year_end, registr_dt, voter_status_desc, voter_status_reason_desc; no birth date)

private_challenge.who: Any registered voter of the county (G.S. 163-85(a)).
private_challenge.form_or_statute: G.S. 163-85: written challenge, under oath, on the State Board form, filed with the county board of elections; ground (c)(7): 'not a citizen of the United States'.
private_challenge.deadlines: No challenge under 163-85 after the 25th day before each primary, general, or special election (163-85(a)). For the November 3, 2026 general election that is October 9, 2026. The board hears it before the election unless volume prevents it (163-86(a)); the voter gets at least 10 days' mailed notice (163-86(b)).
private_challenge.evidence_standard: Burden of proof on the challenger; with no testimony the board dismisses; a full hearing only on probable cause (163-85(d)). Challenges 'shall not be made indiscriminately' and only if the challenger 'knows, suspects or reasonably believes' the person is not qualified (163-90.1(a)). No challenge is sustained without 'affirmative proof'; the presumption is that the voter is properly registered (163-90.1(b)).
private_challenge.false_statement_penalty: Knowingly false affidavit or oath under this Article is a Class I felony (G.S. 163-90.3).

sources.cite: N.C.G.S. 163-90.2 (action when sustained; appeal within 10 days)
N.C.G.S. 163-90.3 (false affidavit is a Class I felony)

state_windows.effect: No challenge may be made after the 25th day before the election.

state_election_office.name: North Carolina State Board of Elections

ag.name: North Carolina Department of Justice (Attorney General)
ag.note: Under G.S. 163-82.14(c1)(1)c the State Board itself sends cases where a prospective juror voted before becoming a citizen to the SBI and the district attorney.

gates.basis: The State Board's noncitizen jury-excusal list is a public record (G.S. 9-6.2(b)). The voter file is public (163-82.10(c)). Private sworn challenges are allowed (163-85). Named export goes only to the referral targets in this file. Challenge guidance shows with the warning that a match alone is not 'affirmative proof' (juryroll_lead_sufficient is null, so the app treats it as false).

notes: Matching limit: the public jury list has date of birth withheld (163-82.10(a1)) and the public voter file has birth year only. No pair can reach the 'full DOB' tier. The app must cap NC matches at Probable (LOGIC-CHANGES.md A.4).

Duplication: the State Board already receives the same list with dates of birth and must review it within 30 days (163-82.14(c1)). A private referral should ask whether that review happened, not re-assert the match.
The State Board excludes people who became citizens after the disqualification date (163-82.14(c1)(1)b). JuryRoll's registration-date check (LOGIC-CHANGES.md B) mirrors this.

A June 2026 consent judgment in a state-court case (reported by Carolina Journal, not checked against the court docket) has the State Board post the list on its FTP site with redactions. Not used as a rule source.
The 163-85 deadline for the November 3, 2026 election is October 9, 2026, two days after verified_on.
no_online_posting is null: the State Board itself posts the voter file publicly, and no bar on re-posting was found in 163-82.10. The app treats null as barred. JuryRoll never posts data.
penalty is null: no misuse penalty for voter lists was found in 163-82.10.

Majority Forward v. Ben Hill County (M.D. Ga. 2021) and Fair Fight v. True the Vote (N.D. Ga. 2024) (LEGAL-REVIEW.md) are federal cases from Georgia, not North Carolina; they show how courts treat mass private challenges in the 90-day window.
